steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: Here are the results of the latest public opinion survey.

steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: The Schwire Group's Aquatic Paradise proposal is supported by 33% of those polled, while the MountainDash Logistics center proposal is supported by 21% of those polled.

steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: The other competitors are all hovering at around 10%.

steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: Although the result of the public opinion survey is only one of the factors that the city government considers when making its decision, based on the current results, the Schwire Group's proposal has the advantage.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Say no more. I'm sure Mr. Bison here can figure out the situation by himself.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Surely Miss Swire didn't invite me and the city government here just to gloat over the results?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Of course not. Bison, sir, I'd like to make a deal.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The Schwire Group will drop out of the bidding, but in return, I want to buy into MountainDash Logistics's company here.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Hasn't that been your goal all along?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Not entirely, but I thought about it little afterwards, and your being here isn't all bad news to me.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: A smart businessperson always looks for possibilities where both parties gain something and makes decisions that yields the maximum profits given the situation.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Going by what you said... If you were really so confident, you wouldn't have come negotiate with me.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, would you not agree that trading a percentage of your shares in exchange for your biggest rival's exit is a good deal?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: How much are you looking at?
Swire lightly knocks on the table three times.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I want this much.

steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: I will report your arrangement to the mayor and continue to inform you of any further arrangements.

steps.name: City Hall Staffer
steps.text: I wish you two a pleasant time in Siesta.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Is that all for the show?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: For the time being, I guess.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Haha... Hahaha...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What's so funny?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Sorry, sorry... I just didn't expect... that you'd resort to these means, too, Commissioner Swire...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: If I were to openly invest in MountainDash's business, forget about registering our own company. They'd write MountainDash up for thousands of reasons and shut it down on our first day in Siesta.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My family's wary of me. Good thing they aren't that wary of me yet. As long as they still see me as a young, hot-headed superintendent, I can still cover my actions with that as a ruse.

spans.text: My family's wary of me. Good thing they aren't
wary of me yet. As long as they still see me as a young, hot-headed superintendent, I can still cover my actions with that as a ruse.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Phew—I'm really fortunate that I'm not actually your business rival.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This is just the first step, though. The Federation of Enterprises will put it all together sooner or later. We'll face all sorts of difficulties going forward. Are you ready?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Having come this far, it's probably too late for me to have any regrets.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, partners, then?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Yeah, I look forward to—

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Your terminal?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No, isn't it yours?
Swire and Bison each take out their terminals. They take a brief look at each other, before hitting their respective answer keys.

steps.name: Polite Voice
steps.text: Hello, is this Bison, the legal representative of Mountaincomm Trade?

steps.name: Hushed Voice
steps.text: Hello, is this Miss Swire?

steps.name: Polite Voice
steps.text: The city hall has received a report that your company has illegally employed undocumented Infected. At this point, we need your company to immediately cease all operations.

steps.name: Polite Voice
steps.text: Please prepare the following documents for the city government's investigation. First, we need the list of all Infected employees working for your company...

steps.name: Hushed Voice
steps.text: Miss Swire, that was an interesting show, and it did buy you some time for your prank. Unfortunately, the group is very unhappy with your decision.

steps.name: Hushed Voice
steps.text: You should know that there are limits to what you should and shouldn't do. This investment game is over.

steps.name: Polite Voice
steps.text: Thank you for your cooperation. Goodbye.

steps.name: Hushed Voice
steps.text: This stops here. I hope you'll think about the consequences of your actions.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: This is some uncalled-for slander.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, it's pretty obvious who snitched on us. They're trying to buy time right before we sign our contract just so they can catch up.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But why use the Infected as an excuse... Since when has Siesta had any policies against the Infected in any way?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: We don't have time to deal with these setbacks.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If only we could convince Mayor Herman—

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You're right. Herman is our chance at a breakthrough, but what reason does he have to stand on our side...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Besides, if my hunch's correct, he's probably being pressured in some other way right now.

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: Mayor Herman, you're a hard man to reach.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: I thought my answer before was more than clear. There is nothing for you and I to discuss in person.

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: Naturally, Columbia respects all the rights that Siesta enjoys as an independent city state. I am here today for a different matter—Siesta's Infected question.

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: Columbian federal law states that Infected citizens must be enrolled in a suitable healthcare plan in order to reside in our nomadic cities. Otherwise, they must join the Pioneer Teams.

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: Siesta was not a nomadic city, and so it was not bound by this regulation. However, given the current circumstances, we need to reevaluate the rule of law here.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: So this word game is your idea of pressuring me?

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: I hope you grasp the situation, Mayor Herman.

steps.name: Columbian Representative
steps.text: This is not a negotiation.

steps.name: Tired Worker
steps.text: Since when do we need to be so sneaky about buying obsidian?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What choice do we have? They've been pretty strict with inspections lately. But this is a great opportunity for people like you, in-the-know, to seize the day!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: The logistics center will be done soon, and there are lots of merchants waiting to buy obsidian.

steps.name: Weary Worker
steps.text: Ugh, when has Siestan obsidian ever been all that rare? You probably have plenty hidden in your shop yourself. Why come to me?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What they want is freshly-mined obsidian. What's it...? Volcano-heated obsidian contains the land's energy and has amazing health benefits!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Alright, I'll stop messing with you. Do you have any other new obsidian pieces, aside from this basket? Whatever you've got, I have buyers lined up. If the quality's good enough, they're willing to pay this much.
Enis gestures a number with his hands.

steps.name: Spirited Worker
steps.text: That much? Yeah, I do. I dug up a bunch just a couple days ago.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Oh? So recently?

steps.name: Spirited Worker
steps.text: Yep. I kept some real pretty ones—Look, these are some mighty fine obsidians, don't you think?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: They're lovely indeed.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Now, would you please tell me more about your illegal obsidian mining operation?

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: Enis! You set me up, didn't you?! When did you fall so low?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Uh, this isn't exactly a set up now, is it? A cop with a really loud mouth taught me this... Sorry, Uncle Jackie. This is for your own good. You shouldn't put your health on the line.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: We just have a couple questions we want to ask you. Work with us, will you?

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: That's everything...

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: Are you gonna lock us up?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Who were you planning to sell the obsidian to?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Is it Pelipper?

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: No... Pelipper stopped buying from us a long time ago, and he's a man of his word. He hasn't bought a single pebble. No matter how high quality the obsidian, he doesn't so much as take a single glance.

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: Hmph... You got all this out of us, but what good is it going to do?

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: That bastard Herman's always doing whatever he wants without a thought to the consequences. First, he made us all stop mining obsidian. Then, he said the volcano was going to erupt. It's been almost two years since we moved here, and it hasn't so much as let out a puff of smoke!

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: Maybe he should've taken a look at where our money was coming from just a couple years ago...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But doesn't Siesta have really lax Infected policies...?

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: That doesn't mean they've got jobs for us! If all the out-of-work miners became drivers, they could probably tow the city a couple kilometers.

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: Besides, I'm already infected. What else can I do? Once MountainDash Logistics moves into the city, we'll have even more people without work. Now the Mayor's talking about tearing the shopping district down. Why tear it down, even? Just to chase us out of here?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Maybe... Maybe the Mayor will come up with a policy to help you guys...

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: Forget it. Haven't you heard? They're going to chase us Infected out. The Columbians are here.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Where did you hear that?

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: We all know how the Columbians treat the Infected. If something does end up happening, we might as well just head out into the wastes ourselves and start pioneering.

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: That shell-brain Herman... That darned shell-brain!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Ugh... *cough*! *cough*!

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: What's wrong? Are you sick?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: No, no. Uh, I...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Uh, Dr. Ceylon, they're also...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: The Mayor must be having a tough time, too. Don't get mad over this...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: No, I'm not mad.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I thought this was just going to be warning a few men to stop illegal mining, but if the Columbians are here, that changes everything...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: This is Siesta's own problem.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Sir, how many are still mining obsidian?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'll come out and say it. I'm not going to turn you in to the police.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Enis said it just now. I'm a doctor. I know it's not realistic to just stop your obsidian work. What I want to do is help you solve this problem... Please trust me.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: So, won't you tell me?

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: What do you mean, you're going to help us?

steps.name: Dispirited Worker
steps.text: Uh, who are you...? And why?

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: Hold on... You look familiar...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Hah, you finally figured out, huh? You watched the Obsidian Festival broadcasts, right? Remember the lady at the closing ceremonies with Mayor Herman?

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: Who? No, no, no. I'm saying you look a lot like a woman I once met...

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: It was a long time ago, and we worked at the obsidian mines together.

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: There was a scholar from Victoria. She was pregnant, but she went to the mines every day, for environmental surveys or whatever.

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: She didn't know that much about mining, but she was real kind to us...

steps.name: Discouraged Worker
steps.text: Oh, now I remember. Her name was... Bora... No, Barbara.
The creature, with the miner's lamp on its back, trots along in short spurts as it gazes toward Old Siesta's beach.
There, Byrd is sitting on the sand, plucking away at her strings spontaneously.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Do you come here often?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hmm, you can still see Old Siesta here...

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Well, music is pleasing to the ear, and the sound of the waves, carried on the wind, is good accompaniment for the guitar.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: I didn't expect you to ask me that, though... So you're actually willing to talk.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Huh? Isn't this what one would normally do...?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Yeah... I guess it is. maybe I'm just a bit too narrow-minded.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: If everything can talk to everything else, then music might be the best language there is. Even if you don't speak the same tongue, music can help you convey your truest thoughts—Not bad. This feels like a new inspiration.
Byrd starts strumming a slow, relaxed song. The waves rise and fall along to her rhythm.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: You two are the first to hear this piece.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'You two?' Oh... Are you including this fowlbeast here? Maybe the grass?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Hm? No.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Don't we have another listener here?
Byrd points at the steps next to them which, logically, should be empty.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Weren't you talking to it the whole time?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Miss Byrd... You can see it?

The creature with a miner's lamp on its back stands on the beach and gazes blankly at the silhouette of Old Siesta in the distance. It hesitantly tries to step into the seawater, but after a few plods, it walks back onto land.
Its takes its hoofsteps rhythmically, as though it is trying to match the music's beat, though it also looks like it isn't and is just trying to maintain its own rhythm.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump...

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Yeah, I've been able to see it since the day I came to Siesta.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Just the one?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Are there others?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Too bad... This is the only one I can see.
Byrd looks at the lamp on the creature's back and the hard hat and goggles on its head.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: I wrote the miners of Old Siesta a song. Maybe it just happens to like things that have to do with ores?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: I'll play the song again, just for it.
Byrd starts strumming again, while Adele brushes her dress's hem and sits down next to Byrd.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Come to think of it, even though there hasn't been a single song of mine that could represent my whole life, perhaps there's one or two that could give comfort to somebody out there...

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: ...even if my audience is just a lone... Little Black Sheep?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: But that's not so bad!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It stayed behind to listen to you play your guitar.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: You said you could see more of them. Where are they?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They... They disappeared all of a sudden. I don't know where they went.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Do they eat road signs like this one?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I don't think so...

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Hm, I have an idea.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Do you think this one eats road signs because... it's a stray sheep?
